title: Coda: on-call handoff + after-action (2027-05-06)
content:
Purpose and context:
Quick handoff notes from the overnight -> day shift. Primary focus: midday latency spike tied to a Canary rollout that started at ~11:15 PDT, follow-ups and recommended runbook edits. This is a working record; please add clarifications inline.

Summary (TL;DR):
- What happened: Canary rollout of v2.4.8 to a subset of Dedicated cluster B caused high tail latency and elevated 5xx rates for the hosted API route /v1/generate between ~11:22–11:55 PDT. Root cause appears to be a change in cache key sharding that increased hot-key pressure and triggered cascading cache evictions on Redis nodes.
- Impact: p99 latency for text-gen rose from ~180ms -> 1.4s, error rate from 0.6% -> 3.2% on affected route. No data loss; no customer-managed private deployments impacted.
- Mitigation: Rolled back Canary at 11:32 PDT (kubectl rollout undo), scaled Redis memory + forced rewarm of prefix cache, and applied a temporary routing rule to divert 10% traffic to fallback model variant. Full mitigation by 11:55 PDT.

Detailed timeline (rough):
- 11:15 PDT: Canary rollout initiated (v2.4.8) — 10% of hosts in cluster B.
- 11:22 PDT: Alerts triggered: routing_slo_p99_high on /v1/generate, several ’redis_evictions’ warnings.
- 11:25 PDT: Pager to on-call (me). Initial hypothesis: model change increased average sequence length, causing larger KV cache footprint.
- 11:27 PDT: Noticed unusual key churn on Redis group redis-primary-2 (node 3) via redis-cli info and our eviction metrics.
- 11:29 PDT: Canary hosts showing elevated CPU on forwarder and slower socket connects (socket_wait_ms p95 increased).
- 11:32 PDT: Decision: rollback Canary -> executed kubectl rollout undo on deployment/redwood-api-service in cluster B.
- 11:34 PDT: Began temporary routing: route 10% to model-variant-stable (fallback) via /routing/api toggle.
- 11:41 PDT: Increased Redis maxmemory on redis-primary-2 from 16GB -> 20GB; performed controlled rewarm (prefetch top prefixes).
- 11:52 PDT: Error and latency trending toward baseline. Monitored until 11:55 PDT.

Commands & checks used (notes):
- kubectl -n prod rollout status deployment/redwood-api-service --watch
- kubectl rollout undo deployment/redwood-api-service -n prod --to-revision=10
- redis-cli -h redis-primary-2 INFO memory | grep used_memory
- PromQL used: sum(rate(http_request_errors_total[5m])) by (route), histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(request_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le, route))
- Verified fallback routing via curl + trace-id to ensure model-variant-stable responses were healthy.

Root cause (current understanding):
- A code change in v2.4.8 altered the cache key format for prefix caching (shard bits moved), which concentrated several high-frequency user prefixes onto fewer Redis hash slots. That increased eviction churn and increased KV lookup latency when misses required recomputation. The change passed unit tests but didn’t exercise production prefix distribution.
- Secondary factor: autoscaling thresholds for Redis group redis-primary-2 are conservative; memory pressure climbed quickly because several other services were using the same node pool for ephemeral workload.

Customer impact notes:
- A few customers reported intermittent 5xxs during 11:20–11:50 PDT. We opened a support ticket bundle and posted to status.redwood.ai (incident page) at 11:38 PDT with a brief summary and an ETA. Follow-up customer comms are handled by CS (Sofia).

Action items (who / what / due):
- (Maya) Draft postmortem stub and link to INFR-4123. Due: 2027-05-10.
- (Tomas) Add a Prometheus alert for redis_eviction_rate > 10/min sustained for 5m. Also add a runbook step to check key distribution on canaries. Due: 2027-05-08.
- (Liam) Revert cache key format patch in infra repo until canary tests include production-ish key distributions. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/571. Due: 2027-05-07 (hotfix).
- (Sofia) Coordinate customer follow-ups for high-visibility accounts and post incident timeline on the status page. Due: 2027-05-07.
- (Janelle) Evaluate Redis node isolation: consider dedicated node pool for hot KV namespaces. Draft recommendation by 2027-05-20.

Runbook edits recommended (quick list):
- Insert a pre-canary checklist: run sample-key-distribution script (tools/canary-key-check) against target cluster to simulate prefix heatmaps. Pass required before canary: distribution CV < 1.8.
- Add step under 'High Redis Evictions' to inspect hash slot distribution and suggestion to scale memory by +20% before rolling back if rollback not desired.
- Add explicit step to toggle fallback routing and verify traces before making rollback decision.

Open questions / notes to follow up:
- Why did the canary tests not surface the distribution issue? Test harness likely uses synthetic prefixes — need to add sampling from production prefix histogram.
- Should we fast-track a canary-only preflight that runs in prod but throttled to a small synthetic user bucket? Security/privacy check required.
- Confirm whether autoscaler for redis-primary groups ought to be more aggressive during canaries.

Unresolved tasks carried forward:
- Update the canary playbook with the sample-key-distribution step (Tomas / Liam).
- Patch verification harness to use sampled real-prefix patterns (Research/Applied-ML to own sampling approach).
- Create a dashboard panel for 'cache-key-skew' and add it to the default SRE on-call view.

Follow-ups I performed briefly while handing off:
- Filed INFR-4123 with initial notes and raw graphs.
- Created quick dashboard snapshot and pinned to on-call channel.
- Notified CS / Solutions for high-touch accounts.

Handoff checklist (for next shift):
- [ ] Confirm INFR-4123 updated with any new logs/graphs you find.
- [ ] Check redis_eviction_rate and p99 latency for /v1/generate for next 12 hours.
- [ ] Validate the hotfix PR status and merge timeline.
- [ ] Review fallback routing metrics to ensure no long-term tail effects.
- [ ] If you see renewed evictions: run redis-cli --latency on node redis-primary-2 and collect top keys using redis-sampler.

Escalation contacts (in order):
- Primary: Tomas Nguyen (infra lead) — pager / cell: oncall-tomas
- Secondary: Liam O'Connor (runtime eng) — Slack @liam
- Redis support escalation: vendor-ops@redwood-redis.com (use INFR-4123 in subject)

Notes to incoming on-call (MORNING SHIFT):
- We rolled back the Canary but the cause is still in code. Treat this as medium-risk for future canaries until key distribution checks are in place.
- Watch for correlated increases in socket_wait and worker CPU on forwarders; those may be early indicators of a hot-key event.
- If you need to perform an emergency rollback and cannot reach the on-call leads, perform the rollback and open a ticket with description and why. Safety-first.

Attachments / artifacts I uploaded:
- pinned graphs: p99_latency_2027-05-06.png, redis_evictions_2027-05-06.png
- logs bundle: s3://redwood-ops/incident-dumps/INFR-4123/

Final note (meta):
This handoff doubles as a draft for the postmortem. I prioritized immediate mitigation first; the action items emphasize preventative tooling (distribution checks, dashboarding) over process only. Please add any missing pieces and flag if we need an all-hands postmortem review.

— Maya R.
